about: Cantina Ortaccio is the tiny natural-wine project of Massimo “Max” Antonuzi and his partner Patrizia Montanari in Latera, a hill village above Lake Bolsena in northern Lazio, about two hours north of Rome. Max’s family has lived in these parts for generations; his grandfather came from nearby Gradoli. Max trained and worked as an architect, then ran a wine bar in Rome from 2003 to 2013, began selling natural wine in 2005, and finally left the bar trade to make wine himself, in a cellar dug directly beneath his house.

Dritto is a wine made from memory. When Max was a teenager, his grandfather gave him 365 bottles of his own skin-fermented Procanico, one for every day of the year, and each vintage Max tries to recreate it. Procanico, the local form of Trebbiano, grows on volcanic soils near the lake shore, planted among olive trees. The grapes are organically farmed and picked by hand. In recent vintages the wine has fermented on its skins with wild yeast for around three weeks, partly in chestnut barrels, and is bottled unfined, unfiltered and with no added sulphur.

Skin contact gives Procanico more texture and grip than a conventional white: expect fruit with a faint tannic edge and fresh acidity rather than a delicate, aromatic wine. Ortaccio’s UK importer describes the Dritto as complex and rich, with an orange-sherbet note, a wine meant for the table that also ages well; older vintages have kept beautifully.
facts: Volcanic, near the shore of Lake Bolsena
Skin-fermented with wild yeast; part finished in chestnut barrels (2021 vintage method)
